gen.title: Bill of Rights Proposal and Ratification Facts

cards.stem: How many amendments were put forward at the start?
cards.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.
cards.hint: Check the first sentence of the introduction

cards.stem: Which body put forward amendments for the states to consider?
options: First Congress of the United States
state conventions in their formal ratification
cards.quote: On September 25, 1789, the First Congress of the United States therefore proposed to the state legislatures 12 amendments to the Constitution
cards.hint: Look for the date and body that proposed amendments

cards.stem: Which articles were approved on that December date by the required share of legislatures?
options: The first amendment, which concerned the number of constituents
cards.quote: Articles 3 to 12, ratified December 15, 1791, by three-fourths of the state legislatures, constitute the first 10 amendments

cards.stem: What later outcome happened to Article 2 about compensation?
options: finally ratified on May 7, 1992 as the 27th Amendment
ratified December 15, 1791, by three-fourths of the state legislatures
cards.quote: was finally ratified on May 7, 1992 as the 27th Amendment to the Constitution.
cards.hint: Think about the compensation article later fate

checks.message: every quiz text length, id pattern and id uniqueness is within the frozen limits
all 4 card quote(s) appear verbatim in their cited source after whitespace normalisation (quote-verbatim)
every card's correct answer options[0] occurs in its quote after normalisation (answer-in-quote)
every card has distinct options after normalisation (options-distinct)
no stem contains its own correct answer (stem-no-answer-leak)
exactly one option per card matches the quote (one-correct)
every number in stems, options and hints appears on the cited page or in the same quote (N-01) (numbers-checkable)
no distractor occurs in its card quote (distractors-not-in-quote)
